Get or set the value of a param

Source: R/param.R
param_value.Rd

Get the plain value of a param or replace it, keeping the rest of the param.

Usage

param_value(x)

param_value(x) <- value

Arguments

x

A param object.

value

The new value.

Value

param_value(): the plain value. param_value<-: the updated param object.

Details

Functions

  • param_value() returns the plain value: the value without label, validity and the other attributes of the param, but with its class (e.g. factor, Date) and structure (e.g. names, dim). For a param_group() it returns a named list of the plain values of its children.

  • param_value<- replaces the value and keeps everything else (label, validity, ...).

Setting a value

The new value is converted to the type of the current one, e.g. a text "2" becomes the number 2 for a numeric param. Also:

  • The names or dimensions of the new value replace those of the current one.

  • A factor param keeps its levels: values outside them become NA, which the validity check of choice_param() reports. A new factor brings its own levels.

  • A date-time param reads texts in its own time zone. ISO 8601 texts with T and a trailing Z (UTC) work too.

  • A param as new value contributes its plain value.

  • A param group takes a named list with (at least) the names of its children.

Examples

p <- choice_param("yes", c("yes", "no"), label = "Question")
param_value(p)
#> [1] yes
#> Levels: yes no
param_value(p) <- "no"
p
#> param<factor>: <factor[1]: no>
#>   levels: yes, no
#>   label: Question
#>   validity: <function>

g <- param_group(list(a = param("x"), b = numeric_param(1)))
param_value(g)
#> $a
#> [1] "x"
#> 
#> $b
#> [1] 1
#> 
param_value(g) <- list(a = "y", b = 2)
param_value(g)
#> $a
#> [1] "y"
#> 
#> $b
#> [1] 2
#> 

# Date-times: texts are read in the time zone of the param
start <- param(
    as.POSIXct("2026-10-05 12:00:00", tz = "Europe/Berlin"),
    label = "Start"
)
param_value(start) <- "2026-10-06 08:30:00"
param_value(start)
#> [1] "2026-10-06 08:30:00 CEST"

# ISO 8601 texts with a trailing Z are UTC (08:30 UTC is 10:30 in Berlin)
param_value(start) <- "2026-10-06T08:30:00Z"
param_value(start)
#> [1] "2026-10-06 10:30:00 CEST"
